title: The Year of the Elephant and the Divine Protection of the Ka'bah
overview: This episode details the historical events leading to the attempted destruction of the Ka'bah by the Abyssinian governor Abrahah. It covers the political shifts in Yemen, the rivalry between the church of al-Qulays and the Ka'bah, and the miraculous intervention of Allah in the Year of the Elephant, which coincided with the birth of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
lessons: Absolute Trust in Allah (Tawakkul): Abdul Muttalib’s reliance on Allah to protect the Ka'bah demonstrates that believers should fulfill their responsibilities while trusting Allah with the ultimate outcome.
The Sacredness of the Ka'bah: The miraculous intervention against Abrahah proves that Allah preserves His sacred symbols and provides protection for the sanctuary of Makkah.
The Consequences of Treachery: The eternal disgrace of Abu Righal serves as a warning against aiding those who seek to destroy the symbols of faith.
Allah's Wisdom in Timing: The destruction of Abrahah's army in the same year as the Prophet's ﷺ birth served as a divine preparation of the land for the final message of Islam.
The Folly of Arrogance: Abrahah's power, army, and elephant were no match for the small, seemingly insignificant creatures sent by Allah.

chapters.title: The Abyssinian Conquest of Yemen
chapters.summary: Following the massacre of 20,000 believers in trenches of fire by the Himyarite king Dhu Nuwas, a survivor named Daws Dhu Tha'laban sought aid from the Byzantine Emperor. The Emperor referred him to the Najashi (Negus) of Abyssinia, who dispatched a massive army of 70,000 soldiers to avenge the Christians. Led by the commanders Aryat and Abrahah, the army successfully overthrew Dhu Nuwas, who committed suicide, marking the transition of Yemen to Abyssinian rule.
key_points: Dhu Nuwas, son of Tibban As'ad, massacred believers in trenches of fire.
Daws Dhu Tha'laban escaped and sought help from the Qaysar (Byzantine Emperor).
Najashi sent an army of 70,000 soldiers under the command of Aryat.
Dhu Nuwas committed suicide by drowning in the sea after his defeat.
Abrahah served as a high-ranking officer in the initial conquest.

chapters.title: The Rise of Abrahah al-Ashram
chapters.summary: After the conquest, Aryat became an oppressive ruler, causing internal dissent within the Abyssinian military. Abrahah led a defecting faction, but to avoid a full-scale civil war that would weaken their presence in Yemen, he challenged Aryat to a one-on-one duel. During the fight, Abrahah's nose was cut, earning him the title al-Ashram, but he ultimately killed Aryat and secured his position as the new ruler. To maintain his legitimacy with the Najashi, Abrahah sent his own hair and soil from Yemen as a sign of submission.
key_points: Aryat's oppression led to a military coup led by Abrahah.
Abrahah proposed a duel to avoid mutual destruction of the Abyssinian army.
Abrahah became known as 'al-Ashram' (the one with the cut nose) during the duel.
Abrahah killed Aryat and became the de facto ruler of Yemen.
The Najashi accepted Abrahah's rule after a strategic display of loyalty.

chapters.title: Al-Qulays and the Provocation of Ahl al-Nasi'
chapters.summary: To demonstrate his loyalty to the Najashi, Abrahah built a magnificent church called al-Qulays in Sana'a, intending for it to replace the Ka'bah as the primary site of pilgrimage. This plan deeply offended the Arabs, particularly a group known as Ahl al-Nasi', who held the authority to manipulate the sacred months. One member of this group defiled the church in protest, which infuriated Abrahah and led him to swear an oath to march on Makkah and destroy the Ka'bah once and for all.
key_points: Abrahah built the elaborate church of al-Qulays in Yemen.
Ahl al-Nasi' were a group of Arabs known for 'delaying' sacred months (nasi').
The four sacred months (al-Ashhur al-Hurum) are Rajab, Dhu al-Qa'dah, Dhu al-Hijjah, and Muharram.
A member of Ahl al-Nasi' defiled al-Qulays to humiliate Abrahah.
Abrahah identified the Ka'bah as the primary obstacle to his church's success.

chapters.title: The March on Makkah and the Treachery of Thaqif
chapters.summary: Abrahah led his vast army toward Makkah, bringing along a great elephant named Mahmud to physically dismantle the Ka'bah. Although Arab leaders like Dhu Nafar and Nufayl al-Khuth'umi attempted to resist him, they were defeated and taken as prisoners. Upon reaching Ta'if, the tribe of Thaqif surrendered out of cowardice and even provided a guide, Abu Righal, to show the way to Makkah. Abu Righal died before reaching the destination, and his grave became a site of symbolic stoning by the Arabs for his treachery.
key_points: Abrahah brought a large elephant named Mahmud to destroy the Ka'bah.
Arab leaders Dhu Nafar and Nufayl al-Khuth'umi were captured after resisting.
The tribe of Thaqif in Ta'if aided Abrahah to save their own city.
Abu Righal served as a guide for the army but died on the outskirts of Makkah.
The Arabs traditionally stone the grave of Abu Righal due to his betrayal.

chapters.title: The Meeting of Abdul Muttalib and Abrahah
chapters.summary: As Abrahah's army reached Makkah, they confiscated 200 camels belonging to Abdul Muttalib, the prestigious leader of the Quraysh. Through the mediation of the elephant trainer Unays, Abdul Muttalib met with Abrahah, who was initially struck by the Arab leader's dignified appearance. To Abrahah's surprise, Abdul Muttalib requested only the return of his camels, explaining that while he was the lord of the camels, the Ka'bah was the House of Allah and He would protect it. Abrahah returned the property and advised the Makkans to evacuate the city.
key_points: Abrahah confiscated 200 camels belonging to Abdul Muttalib.
Abdul Muttalib was the grandfather of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and leader of Makkah.
Unays, the elephant trainer, helped arrange the meeting with Abrahah.
Abdul Muttalib famously stated: 'Inna li-hadha al-bayti rabban yahmih.'
The people of Makkah retreated to the mountains to observe the events.

chapters.title: The Miraculous Destruction of the Army
chapters.summary: When Abrahah ordered his army to attack, the elephant Mahmud miraculously knelt and refused to move toward the Ka'bah. Simultaneously, Allah sent swarms of birds (ababil) carrying small stones that caused the flesh of the soldiers to disintegrate upon impact. The entire army, including Abrahah, was destroyed, an event immortalized in Surah al-Fil. This year became known as the Year of the Elephant (Am al-Fil), serving as a momentous sign and the year in which Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born.
key_points: The elephant Mahmud refused to walk toward the Ka'bah but moved in other directions.
Swarms of birds known as 'ababil' dropped stones on the invading army.
The stones caused the flesh of the soldiers to fall off their bones.
The event is recorded in the Qur'an in Surah al-Fil.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in this year, known as Am al-Fil.

The grand church built by Abrahah in Sana'a, Yemen, to divert pilgrims from Makkah.
A city in the mountains near Makkah, home to the tribe of Thaqif.
Peace be upon him; an honorific used for prophets.
The Year of the Elephant; the year Abrahah attacked Makkah and the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born.
The initial commander of the Abyssinian army sent to Yemen by the Najashi.
The survivor of Dhu Nuwas's massacre who requested help from the Romans and Abyssinians.
The twelfth month of the Islamic calendar and one of the sacred months.
The eleventh month of the Islamic calendar and one of the sacred months.
An Arab noble who resisted Abrahah's army and was taken as a prisoner.
The last Himyarite king of Yemen who persecuted the Christians of Najran.
Abyssinia (modern-day Ethiopia).
Abyssinian; pertaining to Ethiopia.
The Islamic lunar calendar system.
The Prophet Abraham, who built the Ka'bah.
Surely for this House there is a Lord that will protect it; famously said by Abdul Muttalib.
If Allah wills.
Prophet Jesus.

The holy city in the Hijaz where the Ka'bah is located.

Monotheists; those who believe in the oneness of Allah.

An Arab leader who resisted Abrahah and later addressed the elephant Mahmud.

Oppression; injustice.

segments.translit: Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn
Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wanfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā

segments.text: Last week we stopped at the point where the [[Ahabash|أحباش]] or what are modern-day known as the Ethiopians, they took control of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
How did they manage to take control of [[Yemen|اليمن]]?
The king of [[Yemen|اليمن]] whose name was [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] and he was the son of the [[Tubba|تبع]], [[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]], he was an evil man, even though his father was a good man.
[[Tibban As'ad|تبان أسعد]] was a good man, but his youngest son [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he was an evil man.
And he decided to kill those people who believed in Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] by digging big trenches and lighting those trenches on fire,
and those people who wouldn't renounce their belief in Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], they were thrown in that fire.
So it is said on that day that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] killed 20,000 believers. He killed 20,000 believers.
But one of them was able to escape. He killed all of them, but one of them was able to escape and his name was [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس ذُو ثَعْلَبَان]].
And they tried to chase him and they tried to catch him, but he was able to escape and he was a believer in Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
So he wanted to find a solution. What can we do to avenge those people that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] killed? He's only one man.
So he decided to go to the [[Qaysar|قيصر]], and the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] was also a Christian, and he was a very powerful ruler of a Christian empire.
So [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس]] thought that if I go and talk to him, he's a very powerful man, he's much more powerful than the kingdom of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And if he is informed of what [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] did to the Christians who believed in the religion of [[Isa|عِيسَى]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]],
if he is informed of what happened to them and how they were brutally killed by being thrown into ditches of fire, he will definitely do something about it.
So he went to the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] and he told him what happened.
So of course, just as [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس]] expected, the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] was very angry about this and he wanted to do something about it, but he told [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس]]...
He said, "The distance between us and [[Yemen|اليمن]], it's very far. So the more efficient way to deal with this is that I will send some of my people with you..."
"...and you go to Ethiopia, you go to [[Habashah|حباشة]], and talk to the [[Najashi|نجاشي]].

I'll send a letter with you as well, and I will explain to him what you explain to me and he will help you out with this, because the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] of [[Habashah|حباشة]], he was also a Christian."
So [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس]] with the messenger of the [[Qaysar|قيصر]], they went to [[Habashah|حباشة]], and they delivered the message of the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] to [[Najashi|نجاشي]]...
...that [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he did such and such to the Christians of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. He killed them by throwing them into trenches of fire.

So when the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] read this, he was very angry and he was very upset, and in that correspondence, in that letter that the [[Qaysar|قيصر]] sent to [[Najashi|نجاشي]], he said, "Please help this man, please help [[Daws Dhu Tha'laban|دَوْس]]..."
"...to avenge those people who were killed by [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]]." So the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] decided to send a big army to [[Yemen|اليمن]] to avenge the murder of these believers.
So the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] of [[Habashah|حباشة]], he sent a big army under the control or under the authority of a man named [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]]. His name was [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].
He was the commander of the army that [[Najashi|نجاشي]] sent.
And one of the high-ranking officers in that army as well was a man named [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]].
So [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] was the commander of the army and [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was also a high-ranking officer in that army.

So the army moves from [[Habashah|حباشة]] and they go to [[Yemen|اليمن]]. And it's not very far. The distance between [[Habashah|حباشة]] to [[Yemen|اليمن]], it's not very far. So they reach [[Yemen|اليمن]]...
...and this is a huge army. This army that the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] sent, it's an army of 70,000 soldiers. An army of 70,000 soldiers.
This is something that the Yemenis had never seen before. And their forces were not able to even come close to the power that the [[Najashi|نجاشي]]'s army had.
So of course, the [[Najashi|نجاشي]]'s army was victorious under the command of [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]]. They were victorious and they won the battle and they were able to take control of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And that is how [[Yemen|اليمن]] came under control of [[Habashah|حباشة]].
The people of [[Yemen|اليمن]] now, they were not in control of their own land.
So [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he wasn't killed in this battle. He tried to flee. He tried to run away.
So he went to the sea and he tried to board a boat to go into the sea. But they were chasing him. The army of the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] were chasing him.
They wanted to capture him and they wanted to kill him for what he did to those people, for what he did to those Christians.
So they were chasing him and they wanted to catch him and they wanted to execute him.
And when [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]], he was in the sea, when he saw that they were almost about to capture him and he knew that being captured would be inevitable, he knew he had no chance to escape...
...he actually committed suicide.
He jumped into the sea and he drowned himself, because these people felt it was a very dishonorable thing to be captured by the enemy, and they would rather die,
even if that means committing suicide, they would rather kill themselves than be captured from the enemy. So this is how [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]] died.
He committed suicide by drowning himself into the sea.

So that was the end of Yemeni rule to [[Yemen|اليمن]]. Now [[Habashah|حباشة]] has control over [[Yemen|اليمن]]. The Christian empire of Ethiopia, of [[Habashah|حباشة]], they have control over [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] becomes the commander. He's the commander of the military, so he becomes the de facto ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
You know, when a military coup happens, it's the commander of the military who becomes the ruler of the state. So this is exactly what happened in this situation.
[[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]], who was the commander of the [[Habashah|أحباش]] military, he became the head of state in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And sadly, [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] was also a very evil man. He was a very oppressive man. And he did [[zulm|ظلم]] and injustice to not only the Yemenis, but even to his own people.
Like we said, it was an army of 70,000 people. So those 70,000 people now, they're there, they're settled in [[Yemen|اليمن]] as well.
So he's doing [[zulm|ظلم]] on the actual Arabs of [[Yemen|اليمن]] and he's doing [[zulm|ظلم]] on his own people as well. He is an oppressive ruler who doesn't deal with anyone with justice.
So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] is noticing this, that this man now he became powerful, he has rule over the people and he's abusing his power.
He's treating the Yemenis bad and he's even treating us bad, his own people. His own army, he's treating us with oppression and injustice.
So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was able to get a few members of the military to defect to his side, and he wanted to stage a military coup against [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].
And he was able to get a lot of support, a good amount of support from the military, because he was also a pretty high-ranking officer in that military.
So he got ready his army, and [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] got ready those people who stayed in support of him, and they prepared for civil war.
So it was one part of the [[Habashah|أحباش]] army against the other part of the [[Habashah|أحباش]] army. And the Yemenis, the locals, they had nothing to do with this.
It was one group of [[Habashah|أحباش]] against another group of [[Habashah|أحباش]].
The people who stayed in support of [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] against the people who defected to the side of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]. So they got ready to fight.
But before they started the battle, [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] requested to have a face-to-face meeting with [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].
Perhaps they could discuss this in a civilized way and perhaps they could come to some type of a solution without actually having to fight.

So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] requests a meeting with [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] without any weapons. [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] says, "I will take off my weapons and you take off your weapons, and we will just talk man-to-man."

So [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] agrees to this. So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] sit down and they have a conversation. So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] tells [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]], he says, "Look, if we fight, this will be our own..."
our own people destroying our own people. And the [[Yemenis|اليمن]],
they have nothing to do with this.
So you, your forces are going to kill my people, and my forces are going to kill your people. In the end,
we are both going to be the losers.
Because then the [[Ahabash|أحباش]] dominion of this nation will become so weak because we will have lost so many men
that the [[Yemenis|اليمن]] again, they're going to come and they're going to take over their land.
So if we fight, no matter what the outcome, whether you win or I win, in the end both of us are going to lose.
Because we will be so weakened by this war that the [[Yemenis|اليمن]] are going to take over again.
So this is not in your interest or my interest that we actually fight.
We shouldn't fight in this way, with our armies fighting each other.
So [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] says, 'Yes, this makes sense what you're saying.
But what is your solution? How do we solve this problem between you and me?'
He said, 'Instead of having our armies fight each other,
let you and me fight each other one-on-one. We'll have a duel.
Forget about the armies. You and me, man-to-man.'
So [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] says, 'Okay, I agree to it.'
So they both get their weapons ready, and they fight. They fight a duel.
And in the beginning of the fight,
[[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]], he is able to
get a good hit on [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]].
He tries to cut off his neck, but [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] is able to move just in time, and instead of cutting his neck,
his nose gets cut. So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s nose gets cut off.
And that's why he became known after that as [[Abrahah al-Ashram|أَبْرَهَة الأشرم]],
meaning [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], the one with the cut nose.
So he lost his nose early on in the duel, but he was able to overcome that,
and towards the end of the fight, he was able to get power over [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].
He was able to overcome him, and in the end [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] defeated [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].
[[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] killed [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].
So now [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] is gone. [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] is victorious. None of the army is hurt or killed because they didn't even fight.
And [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] becomes the new ruler of [[Yemen|اليمن]]. So now [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] is in charge of [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And he has a huge army at his disposal as well, because they didn't even fight.
So he rules [[Yemen|اليمن]] in this way.
Eventually, news of what happened between [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]], it reaches the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] back in [[Habashah|أحباش]].
And when the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] hears this news that his commander that he put in charge to rule [[Yemen|اليمن]] was killed by another member of the same military,
when [[Najashi|نجاشي]] gets this message and he hears this news, he becomes very angry.
He says, 'How dare [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] thinks that he can kill the one that I appointed to rule that land?
He is overstepping his bounds, and he is trying to go over my authority, because I am the one who put [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] in charge.
So what right did he have to to organize some of the members of the army against him and try to fight him, and eventually he actually killed him
without even taking any counsel or permission from me?' So [[Najashi|نجاشي]] was very, very angry, he was very mad.
And he swore, he made an oath. He said, 'I will go to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
I will not come back to [[Habashah|أحباش]]...
...he swore, he swore 'I will not come back to [[Habashah|أحباش]] until with my own two feet I step on the dirt of [[Yemen|اليمن]]
and I take the hair of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] off of his head.'
And this was considered a sign of humiliation. When they wanted to humiliate a person, they would shave their head and take the hair. This was considered a sign of humiliating someone.
So because [[Najashi|نجاشي]] was so mad, he said, 'I will myself go and step on the earth of [[Yemen|اليمن]], I will step on the dirt of [[Yemen|اليمن]] with my own two feet,
and I will take the hair of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] to humiliate him.'
So he organized his army. He sent 70,000 people of his army to [[Yemen|اليمن]], but he still had a huge army at his disposal back there in [[Habashah|أحباش]].
So he prepared his army to go into [[Yemen|اليمن]].
Before he was near [[Yemen|اليمن]], before he entered [[Yemen|اليمن]],
the news came to [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] that yes, [[Najashi|نجاشي]] is coming, and he's really mad, and this is what he's planning to do to you.
He made an oath that he would not return to [[Habashah|أحباش]] until he with his own two feet stepped on the earth of [[Yemen|اليمن]] and got your hair.
So now [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] is very scared, he panicked. He said, 'Oh, what am I going to do?
There's no way that I will be able to withstand the forces of the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] himself.'
So he made up a plan. He said, 'Okay.' He took some of the dirt of [[Yemen|اليمن]] himself,
and he shaved his own hair himself.
Then he sent a messenger to go and meet the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] before he entered [[Yemen|اليمن]].
He said, 'Take my hair that I just shaved, and take this sample of the earth of [[Yemen|اليمن]] and go to [[Najashi|نجاشي]] before he enters [[Yemen|اليمن]].
And give him my message. My message is that, ya [[Najashi|نجاشي]], I have the utmost loyalty and respect for you, and I am still your follower and I am your servant.
But the only reason why I did this to [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] is because he was doing [[zulm|ظلم]], he was doing oppression on your own people, on your army.
[[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]] was oppressing them and treating them unjustly. So I did this, you know, for our own people, and I did this in service of you.'
So he kissed up to him basically in this message. And the [[Najashi|نجاشي]],
he accepted it.
And then he continued on in the message saying, 'Look, I have sent my hair to you and I have sent some sample of the earth of [[Yemen|اليمن]], so you don't have to even break your oath.
You have my hair and you have the dirt of [[Yemen|اليمن]], just put your feet on it, step on it, and you will have fulfilled your oath.
So you don't have to even come if you accept this.'
And [[Najashi|نجاشي]], he was actually satisfied with this. He said, 'Yeah,
he seems to still be loyal to me.
And you know, if I go into [[Yemen|اليمن]] and we fight, then there will be a lot of bloodshed, a lot of innocent people are going to die.
There's really no need to do this. He seems to still have much loyalty towards me, and I don't think he is going to betray me, so okay, let him lead [[Yemen|اليمن]].
Let him stay in charge of [[Yemen|اليمن]].' And the [[Najashi|نجاشي]], he went back.
[[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] was relieved, of course, but he still had some fear in his heart,
because of course, this was all done through the messenger. [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and the [[Najashi|النجاشي]], they didn't meet face-to-face for this meeting.
So he was still kind of afraid. He was like, "Okay, things are calmed down for now,
but maybe the [[Najashi|النجاشي]], he's planning something.
Maybe he's just keeping the status quo for now, but eventually he's going to come and try to get me out of rule, and he's going to try to replace me or something."
So this paranoia and this fear started developing in [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]].
So he wanted to do something to show the [[Najashi|النجاشي]] what high esteem he holds him in,
what high respect and veneration he has for the [[Najashi|النجاشي]]. He wanted to do something to symbolize his loyalty towards the [[Najashi|النجاشي]].
So he orders for a huge church to be built in [[Yemen|اليمن]].
[[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] orders for a big church to be built in [[Yemen|اليمن]], very big and very intricate, and, you know, very dazzling, this church.
and he sent a message to the [[Najashi|النجاشي]]. He said, "Ya [[Najashi|نجاشي]], I built this huge, beautiful church in [[Yemen|اليمن]] for you,
in your honor, and I am going to order all of the Arabs, from the different tribes of the Arabs,
to come and make pilgrimage to this church.
I'm going to order all of them to make pilgrimage to this church. The Arabs should come and make pilgrimage to this church, and this is an honor to you, ya [[Najashi|نجاشي]]."
So he wanted to do this just to show his respect for the [[Najashi|النجاشي]], so the [[Najashi|النجاشي]] would not do anything to take away his rule.
So he built this church, and he actually tried to order the different tribes of the Arabs to come and make pilgrimage to this church.
So he sent the orders to the different tribes of the Arabs.
And one of the groups of the Arabs that this order reached,
And the word [[nasi'|نسيء]] in Arabic, it means delay.
even though they were not [[Muwahhidin|مُوَحِّدِين]], they were not people of [[tawhid|توحيد]].
And you know that the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was built by [[Ibrahim|إبراهيم]] [[alayhis-salam|عليه السلام]],
and then after many years, [[shirk|شرك]] came back into the Arabian Peninsula, as we spoke about before.
They used to do all of these things. So they still kept their respect for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] even though they were [[mushrikin|مشركين]].
They associated partners and idols with Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
So [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]] were a group of Arabs who had the utmost respect for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], and they were well respected amongst the Arabs as well.
The Arabs gave them a very high position, these people.
And the reason why they were called [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]], and we said [[nasi'|نسيء]], it means delay,
is because there were four months, and there still are four months in the calendar that are considered [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأشهر الحرم]]. They are sacred months.
And those months are [[Rajab|رجب]], [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذو القعدة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذو الحجة]], and [[Muharram|محرم]]. These are called [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأشهر الحرم]].
And Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] made these four months holy and sacred the day that He created the heavens and the earth.

Surely the number of months with Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is twelve months from the day that He created the heavens and the earth, out of these twelve months four of them are sacred.
And from the sacredness of those four months is that it is not allowed to start a war or start fighting during those four months.
Defense is okay. If somebody aggressed upon you, and somebody started a war against you, you have the right to fight back and defend yourself.
But during those four months it's not allowed to start the fighting.
So the Arabs, as you know, as you probably know from the last few weeks that we have been talking about their history, they were a people who always were involved in some type of fighting.
Some type of war was always going on. This is the way that they lived their lives.

So these four months, [[al-Ashhur al-Hurum|الأشهر الحرم]], [[Rajab|رجب]], [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذو القعدة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذو الحجة]], and [[Muharram|محرم]]. [[Rajab|رجب]] is separate. [[Rajab|رجب]] is on its own.
But the other three, [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذو القعدة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذو الحجة]], and [[Muharram|محرم]], they all come consecutively, in a row.
So three consecutive months without any fighting, it was very difficult for the Arabs to be patient and not fight for three consecutive months.
So they wanted to find a way to get around this prohibition. So they appointed this group of Arabs
that with their permission, they could switch [[Muharram|محرم]] and [[Safar|صفر]].

So instead of [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذو القعدة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذو الحجة]], [[Muharram|محرم]], if the [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]], if this group of Arabs, if they agree in certain years, they can switch [[Muharram|محرم]] and [[Safar|صفر]].

So it will be [[Dhu al-Qa'dah|ذو القعدة]], [[Dhu al-Hijjah|ذو الحجة]], two months no fighting, but if they really needed to fight after that, then okay, no [[Muharram|محرم]], it will be [[Safar|صفر]] first, and then after that [[Muharram|محرم]] will come.

So they can switch the place of [[Muharram|محرم]] and [[Safar|صفر]]. Can you believe the way that these people tried to play around with the [[din|دِين]] of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]]?
So the people that were given the authority by the Arabs to do this, they became known as [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]].
And if they decided to switch [[Muharram|محرم]] and [[Safar|صفر]], they would do that.
So these people, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] says about them: 'Surely [[nasi'|نسيء]] is an addition to disbelief.' They're already [[kuffar|كفار]], they're not even Muslims.
But doing this, playing this game of [[nasi'|نسيء]], of delaying, delaying [[Muharram|محرم]] until after [[Safar|صفر]] and switching the places, this is an addition to their [[kufr|كفر]].
They're already [[kuffar|كفار]], and on top of that, they're also doing [[nasi'|نسيء]], they're also playing around with the months.
So this group of Arabs, they were known as [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]], and they used to play this game.
They were the ones who the Arabs used to go to to get that permission to play around with the months like this, and they became known as [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]].
And they were known as the people who had the greatest respect for the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], they had respect for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So when this order from [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] [[al-Ashram|الأشرم]], when it reached the [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]], and these were the people who had great respect for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]],

so they're getting this order, 'You have to go to [[Yemen|اليمن]] and you have to make a pilgrimage to [[al-Qulays|قليس]].' [[al-Qulays|قليس]] was the name of the church that [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] had built.
'So you have to come and you have to make pilgrimage to [[al-Qulays|قليس]].' So when they received this order, they were like, 'What is this [[al-Qulays|قليس]]?
He thinks we're going to come and we're going to make pilgrimage to [[al-Qulays|قليس]], to this church that he built? He thinks that that can take the place of the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]?'
They got very angry, they got offended. How dare he thinks that we're going to do something like this.
So one of them, one of the [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]], he sneaked into [[Yemen|اليمن]], and he went to [[al-Qulays|قليس]] in the night when nobody was around,
and he entered it, and he used the bathroom. He defecated in there, right in the open there.
And then he took that defecation of his, and he rubbed it all over the walls and, you know, the sides of the church and everything. He basically defiled the whole place,
to humiliate [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and to humiliate this place that he thought he could order the people to make pilgrimage to.

So when [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] came to know about it, and he came and he saw it, he saw what actually happened to this place that he built and how it had been defiled, he asked angrily, 'Who did this?'
And then it was said, 'It was someone from [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]].'
And then he said, 'Who are they? Who are [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]]?'
And then it was replied to him, 'They are a group of the Arabs who have a great veneration and respect for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].'
Then [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] asked, 'What is the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]? What are you talking about?'
He said, 'It is the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] that the Arabs, they make pilgrimage to it every year.'
So when [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] heard this, he knew that the Arabs who have such great respect for the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they would never accept his command,
they would never follow his order to make pilgrimage to [[al-Qulays|قليس]] unless the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was destroyed.
So he saw that the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] was an impediment in his way to get the people to come and make pilgrimage to [[al-Qulays|قليس]].
So from that point he decided that he would destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. He decided to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
So he gathered an army with the intention to go to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] and to destroy the House of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]], to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].

And with him, he took an elephant with him. [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] took an elephant with him on his journey from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and the name of this elephant was [[Mahmud|محمود]].
And when he left [[Yemen|اليمن]], [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] kept his son in charge. He kept his son in charge of [[Yemen|اليمن]] while he left to go to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So he organized a big army, he took this elephant [[Mahmud|محمود]], and they were on their way to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now of course, the Arabs, they are aware of what [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] is trying to do. It's not a secret.
They know that he's coming from [[Yemen|اليمن]] on the way to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]. And the Arabs, they were not going to let him do this without a fight.
They were not going to just say, 'Okay, go ahead and do it.' No.
They were going to put their utmost resistance against him and try their best to stop him from doing this. But as we know, [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] commanded a very strong army.
His army was not a small army, it was a big and powerful army.
So on his way, he's going from [[Yemen|اليمن]] on the way to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], there was a man, a great man from the Arabs, he was a very well-respected man, his name was [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]].
And [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]],
he had a small army of Arabs, and they said that, 'Okay, whatever happens, we know that his army is much bigger than ours, but we can't just let him go unimpeded.
We have to try, we have to do something.'
So on his way from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the army, the small army of [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]] confronted [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]. And they fought.
They fought. And [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s army was easily able to overcome the army of [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]]. So they took [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]] as a prisoner.
They didn't kill him, but they took him as a prisoner and they made him accompany them on the way to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. So he was a prisoner now with them.
So they continue to go on the path, and [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]] is with them as well as a prisoner.
Now another group of Arabs also stops them and tries to fight them on the way.
And the leader of this group, he was a man named [[Nufayl al-Khuth'umi|نُفَيْل الخُثْعَمِي]], and he had a group of people from his tribe, from the tribe of [[Khuth'am|خَثْعَم]],
who tried to stop [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] from continuing on his way to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
But again, [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s army was able to overcome them as well, and they took [[Nufayl al-Khuth'umi|نُفَيْل الخُثْعَمِي]] as a prisoner as well.
So now they have [[Dhu Nafar|ذو نفر]] and they have [[Nufayl al-Khuth'umi|نُفَيْل]].
So they have [[Nufayl al-Khuth'umi|Nufayl al-Khuth'ami]] and they have [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]] as
two prisoners on their way.
So they continue on their way.
So they're very close to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] now, [[al-Ta'if|الطَّائِف]] is not far from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
Now when they reach [[al-Ta'if|Ta'if]],
the sad thing is
that the people of [[al-Ta'if|Ta'if]], they showed a very
they showed a very cowardly response to [[Abrahah|Abrahah]].
They were afraid for themselves, they didn't want [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] to destroy their city and kill their people.
So they said, 'Okay, you want to go to [[Makkah|Makkah]] and destroy [[Makkah|Makkah]]? We're not going to stand in your way. You go right ahead
and do that.'
And the extent of their treason
was so much
that they actually offered [[Abrahah|Abrahah]],
they said, 'We'll even send one of our people to go with you
to show you how to get to [[Makkah|Makkah]], to show you [[Makkah|Makkah]] from here.'
So there was a man named [[Abu Righal|أَبُو رِغَال]].
[[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]], he actually volunteered, he said, 'Yeah, I'll go with them, I'll show them [[Makkah|Makkah]], no problem.'
So this was a huge treachery and betrayal
that these people showed and specifically [[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]].
So [[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]], he accompanies the army of [[Abrahah|Abrahah]],
and they're going from [[al-Ta'if|Ta'if]] towards [[Makkah|Makkah]], and [[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]] is actually showing them the way, how to get to [[Makkah|Makkah]].
He really guides them as he said he would.
And just before they reach [[Makkah|Makkah]], they're close to [[Makkah|Makkah]],
[[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]], he dies, Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] caused him to die, and he is buried there.
[[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]] is buried on the way from [[al-Ta'if|Ta'if]] to [[Makkah|Makkah]], and later on in
the years that came,
the place where [[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]] was buried, his grave, it became a place where the Arabs would come to stone.
They would come to the grave of [[Abu Righal|Abu Righal]] and they would stone that grave,

because of this man's betrayal and his treachery that he helped the enemies of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] try to come and destroy the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
So it became a place where the Arabs would come and stone.
So finally,
[[Abrahah|Abrahah]], he reaches the outskirts of [[Makkah|Makkah]] with his big army, and on the outskirts of [[Makkah|Makkah]],
there are people grazing their camels.
There are people that are grazing their camels.
And [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] and his army, they seize all of those camels, they take all of those camels, and included in those camels
were 200 camels of [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]],
200 camels of [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]], and you know who [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] is, he is the grandfather of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.
So 200 camels of [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] and other camels for the other people of [[Makkah|Makkah]], [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] and his army, they confiscate all of them and they take them.
And they come into [[Makkah|Makkah]].
[[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]], he sees what's happening, he sees this [[Habashi|حَبَشِي]] man with a huge army, he has come into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
and he wants to have a face-to-face meeting with [[Abrahah|Abrahah]].
So he tries to arrange a meeting. He said, 'I am the leader of the people of [[Makkah|Makkah]],' and [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]], he was the leader of [[Makkah|Makkah]] without any question.
I mean nobody even would think of coming towards his place in authority.
[[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] was without question the leader of [[Makkah|Makkah]] and everyone of [[Makkah|Makkah]], they respected him as their leader.
So as the leader of [[Makkah|Makkah]], [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] requested a face-to-face meeting with
the commander of this army that had come in, [[Abrahah|Abrahah]].
But [[Abrahah|Abrahah]], he refused to meet anyone. [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] said, 'No, I'm not interested to meet anyone.
I'm going to do what I came to do here,
destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].'
So he refuses this meeting, and [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]], he doesn't know what to do.
He really wants to talk to him.
So he goes to [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]]. [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]], as we mentioned,
he was the first prisoner that [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] had taken on his way from [[Yemen|اليمن]] to [[Makkah|Makkah]].
So he's still there with the army and he's still imprisoned. So [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]], he goes to [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]]
and he says to [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]],
he says, 'You know, I really want to meet [[Abrahah|Abrahah]]. Do you have any suggestions for me?
You have been accompanying this army and these people, you know, for a long time now.
So maybe you have some idea, what can I do to get a face-to-face meeting with [[Abrahah|Abrahah]]?'
And then [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]] says, 'You know, I'm just a prisoner, I really can't do anything myself, but I have one idea for you.
I have noticed while I'm traveling with this army
that [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] is very close to
the one who is in charge of the elephant, the elephant trainer.
Remember [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] had an elephant with him, and with that elephant, he had someone who knew how to command the elephant.
They had someone who was experienced in ordering elephants, and this man's name was [[Unays|أنيس]].
So
[[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]] tells [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] that, 'I noticed that [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] is very close to [[Unays|أنيس]].
[[Abrahah|Abrahah]], he's very close to that elephant trainer [[Unays|أنيس]].
So
if you can get [[Unays|أنيس]] to arrange a meeting between [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] and yourself, I think it will work. And
I can probably talk to [[Unays|أنيس]] about this on your behalf, because during our travels, during our walks, during
this journey that we have gone from [[Yemen|اليمن]] all the way to [[Makkah|Makkah]],
I have also had some conversations with [[Unays|أنيس]],
and you know, we have been able to speak, and he listens to me and we talk sometimes, so maybe
I can talk to [[Unays|أنيس]],
and [[Unays|أنيس]] can talk to [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] to arrange a meeting with you.'
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] says, 'Okay, please, please try to do that.'
So [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]] says, 'Okay.'
And [[Dhu Nafar|Dhu Nafar]] talks to [[Unays|أنيس]] and he says, 'You know, this leader of these people in this city of [[Makkah|Makkah]],
he wants to have a meeting with [[Abrahah|Abrahah]], so maybe you can talk to [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] and maybe he will agree if you tell him.'
So [[Unays|أنيس]] goes back to [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] and [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] agrees. He says, 'Okay, I'll meet with him.'
So when [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] came to meet [[Abrahah|Abrahah]], [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] was sitting on a throne, on a portable throne that they used to carry with them on their travels.
So [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] is sitting up on that throne.
When [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] comes in and [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] sees him for the first time,
he is struck with awe. [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] was a person if you just see him,
you will automatically have reverence and respect for this man. Some people you just see them and you automatically feel a respect for them.
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] was one of these type of people.
He was very handsome, very good looking, and he just commanded a type of respect
to everyone that just laid eyes on him, they automatically respected him.
So
when he came in the room and [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] saw him,
[[Abrahah|Abrahah]] actually got off of his throne and he sat down on the floor with [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]].
He didn't tell [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] to sit down while he stayed on his throne. Out of respect, he actually sat down himself and sat with [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] on the floor.
So then [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] asked him, 'Yes, you wanted to speak to me, what do you want?'
And [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] said, 'You know, when you came into the city,
the people were grazing their camels,
and your army, they confiscated all of those camels, and included in those camels were 200 of my camels.
So I just came here to ask you to please give us our camels back, that's it.'
So then [[Abrahah|Abrahah]], he's surprised, because he was expecting something else, and he's also angry.
He felt disrespected by this.
He said, 'You know, when you came into this room, I had respect for you by seeing you, but now you ask me this type of a question?
You know I came here to destroy the house that you guys go to to worship Allah.
I came to destroy that house,
and all you can ask me about is your camels?
What is this?'
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]] said,
'You know, these camels, they are my camels and my people's camels, this is our responsibility, we are the owners and we have to take care of these things.
So that's why I am asking you for this. As for the house that you want to destroy,
that is the house of Allah.'

segments.translit: Inna li-hadha al-bayti rabban yahmih Target Language Meaning: Surely for this House there is a Lord that will protect it.

segments.text: 'Surely for this house, for the house of Allah, there is a Lord that will protect it. I don't need to protect it. You want to go and try to destroy it?
You know, that's not my business. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is the owner of that house
and he will take care of his house. So I'm not worried about that, I'm just worried about my camels and my people's camels.
So will you release our camels?'
And [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] agrees. He says, 'Okay, I'll release your camels. You can have your camels.'
And then [[Abrahah|Abrahah]] continues to say to [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]],
he says, 'You know,
I didn't come here to hurt you or to hurt your people or to kill anyone,
I don't want to harm anyone. I just came here for one purpose: to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]].
I will destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]] and then I will leave, and you guys can go back to your life, okay?

So while I'm here and while we're destroying the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], I advise you and all the people of [[Makkah|Makkah]], just leave the city, leave [[Makkah|Makkah]] for now, let us do what we want to do,
and then once we leave, come back in, go on with your lives.'
So [[Abdul Muttalib|عبد المطلب]],
he goes out and he orders all of the people of [[Makkah|Makkah]], he says, 'Leave [[Makkah|Makkah]], get out of the city.'
So they all leave the city and they go onto the mountains, you know [[Makkah|Makkah]] is a city that is surrounded by mountains,
So they all go up on the mountain so they can still see what's going on.
So [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army now, they start their mission to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]]. So they come close to the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].

And the elephant that is with them, [[Mahmud|مَحْمُود]], [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] orders the elephant to go and start with the destruction of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], to go to the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] and start breaking it down, this huge elephant.
So the elephant actually gets up and it starts walking in the direction of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
At this point, [[Nufayl al-Khuth'umi|نُفَيْل]], [[Nufayl al-Khuth'umi|نُفَيْل الْخَثْعَمِي]], the second prisoner who they had taken with them, he is able to get loose from his chains.
He's able to get loose from his chains just as [[Mahmud|مَحْمُود]], the elephant, is walking towards the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], and he runs up to [[Mahmud|مَحْمُود]], to the elephant.
And he says, '[[Ya Mahmud|يَا مَحْمُود]], kneel down. This is the house of Allah. This is the house of Allah, kneel down. Don't do it.'
So immediately when he says this, [[Mahmud|مَحْمُود]], he sits down.
And they try to get him up, and he refuses to get up.
So [[Unays|أُنَيْس]], the trainer of the elephant, he comes to him and he tries to get him up, and finally he's able to get him up. So the elephant gets back up.
And then they order him to continue moving forward, but now he won't move forward. He's up, but he won't move forward towards the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
And when the trainer, when [[Unays|أُنَيْس]], turns him in another direction towards [[Yemen|الْيَمَن]] or towards the right or towards the left, he walks. He walks in every direction.
But when you face him towards the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], he doesn't walk, he just stands still.
So they start to get confused, 'Okay, what are we going to do now?'
Their whole reason why they got this elephant is so that it would start in the destruction of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]].
So while they're trying to figure out what to do about this elephant, they see some darkness in the sky, like some big black cloud-like thing, a swarm coming in the sky.
And when it comes closer, they realize that it is these small birds coming, and these are the [[ababil|أَبَابِيل]].
And each one of these birds, they had three stones with them, one in the mouth and one in each one of the legs.
So they come, and that's a huge army, huge, huge army. But a huge, huge number of birds as well.
So they drop those stones on the members of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s army.
And when a stone hits any one of them, what happens is that the meat and the flesh on the body of that person, it just like falls off of their bones.
The stone hits them, and the meat, the flesh, it just dissociates itself from the body, and they die like that.
So now [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]], he's seeing this happening to his army. He isn't hit yet, but he sees this, these stones raining down and all of his army dying immediately.
So he tries to make a run for it, he tries to escape.
But while he is trying to escape, he gets hit by a stone as well, and he is destroyed as well.
Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed every single member of [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s army, including [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] himself.
And it was witnessed by all of the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] from around those mountains. They saw this happen.
And of course, it increased their respect for the house of Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]].
And Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] mentions this incident in the Qur'an:
So this surah is about this incident, of how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army.
And the Arabs in those days, they didn't have a numerical calendar. The years that they had, they weren't numbered.
Like for example, in the Gregorian calendar this year we're in 2016, in the [[Hijri|هِجْرِي]] calendar it's 1438.
But in those days, no, they didn't use to have a numerical year like that.
They used to name the years according to incidents that happened in those years.
So the year that this happened was known as [[Am al-Fil|عَام الْفِيل]], the Year of the Elephant.
[[Am al-Fil|عَام الْفِيل]], so they would say, 'Oh yeah, this incident happened in [[Am al-Fil|عَام الْفِيل]]. This incident happened two years before [[Am al-Fil|عَام الْفِيل]].
This incident happened three years after [[Am al-Fil|عَام الْفِيل]].'
So any big incident that would happen, they would condition their calendar around those incidents.
So [[Am al-Fil|عَام الْفِيل]], the incident of the elephant, it was a huge incident in the history of the Arabs.
So it was a significant event that became a major part of their calendar.
And one of the great significances of this year is that it is the year that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ, was born in this year.
The year that [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] tried to come and destroy the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], the year that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] destroyed [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] and his army,
the year that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] protected His house, this is the year that the greatest man that ever walked on the face of this earth was born.
The year of the birth of Muhammad ﷺ. And [[insha'Allah|إن شاء الله]] next week, we will get into that [[bi-idhnillah|بإذن الله]].

segments.translit: Wa-Allahu a'lam. Wa sallallahu wa sallama wa baraka 'ala nabiyyina Muhammadin wa 'ala alihi wa sahbihi ajma'in.

review.q: Why did [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] decide to march on [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to destroy the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]]?
review.a: He was infuriated after a member of [[Ahl al-Nasi'|أهل النسيء]] defiled his grand church, [[al-Qulays|قليس]], in protest of his plan to divert pilgrims there.

review.q: Who was [[Abu Righal|أبو رغال]] and why is his grave symbolically stoned?
review.a: He was a guide from the tribe of [[Thaqif|ثقيف]] who led the army to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and he is remembered as a traitor to the Arabs.

review.q: How did [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]] receive the title [[Abrahah al-Ashram|أَبْرَهَة الأشرم]]?
review.a: He earned the nickname, which means "the one with the cut nose," during a one-on-one duel with the commander [[Aryat|أَرْيَاط]].

review.q: What reason did [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] give for only asking for his 200 camels?
review.a: He famously stated [[Inna li-hadha al-bayti rabban yahmih|إِنَّ لِلْهَذَا الْبَيْتِ رَبًّا يَحْمِيهِ]], meaning that while he owned the camels, the House had its own Lord to protect it.

review.q: What miracle involving the elephant [[Mahmud|محمود]] occurred during the attack?
review.a: The elephant knelt and refused to move toward the [[Ka'bah|كعبة]], although he would move if turned in any other direction.

review.q: Why did the [[Najashi|نجاشي]] initially send an army of 70,000 soldiers to [[Yemen|اليمن]]?
review.a: The army was dispatched to avenge the massacre of 20,000 believers who were killed in trenches of fire by the king [[Dhu Nuwas|ذو نواس]].

review.q: What were the [[ababil|أَبَابِيل]] and what was their role in the story?
review.a: They were swarms of birds sent by Allah that dropped small stones on [[Abrahah|أَبْرَهَة]]'s army, causing the soldiers' flesh to disintegrate.

review.q: What lesson is drawn from the timing of the destruction of the army in [[Am al-Fil|عام الفيل]]?
review.a: It served as divine preparation of the land for the birth of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] and the coming of the final message of Islam.
